issue.title: internal: Add `--num-threads` to `lsif`
issue.body:
`rust-analyzer lsif` loads the workspace without priming caches and lets `StaticIndex::compute` infer every body lazily on one thread, which dominates the run time on large workspaces.

With `--num-threads N` (N > 1; the default stays 1), `lsif` now primes caches on N threads, as `scip` does, and infers the bodies of all workspace crates on a rayon pool of N threads before the serial walk, as `analysis-stats --parallel` does. The walk then reuses the memoized results, so the dump is unchanged. The default of 1 keeps the previous behaviour and memory use.

issue.title: fix: Panic on `for<'a>` on types using `#[derive()]`
issue.body:
Previously, it was possible for r-a to panic on types that have both a binder and a projection. The unit test added in this commit would panic with the following:

    `Alias(AliasTy { args: [#0, '^1_0.Named(AdtId("S")), '^0.Named(AdtId("S"))], kind: Projection { def_id: TypeAliasId("Item") }, .. }): Clone` has escaping bound vars, so it cannot be wrapped in a dummy binder.

This was because ProjectionFinder was discarding binders, so we'd end up treating `for<'a> F::Bar<'a>` as just `F::Bar<'a>` and panic when `Binder::dummy()` checks for escaping variables.

Instead, collect binders as we walk field types, following the pattern of `bound_generic_params_stack` in `find_type_parameters` in rustc:

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/ac62df9b49f9b9036af2a4957db70bf3850785e1/compiler/rustc_builtin_macros/src/deriving/generic/mod.rs#L404-L471

Since a clause can only have one binder, define a FlattenBinders helper so we use the correct indices when we encounter e.g. `for<'a> for<'b> F::Bar<'a, 'b>`. This follows the pattern elsewhere in r-a (e.g. BoundVarReplacer or the canonicalizer).

issue.title: fix: Large u128 values should not const eval to negative floats

labels.name: repo-2855534c
labels.description: Status: Awaiting review from the assignee but also interested parties.

issue.body:
Previously, we called i128::from_le_bytes() unconditionally, even for u128, so large u128 values would be treated as negative values.

Instead, respect the signedness of the integer type when casting. This seems like it's obviously the correct thing to do, but for reference here's the equivalent rustc logic:

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/fb5f32bdbe75e9114c62589cb86ace65f14a5b78/compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/interpret/cast.rs#L328-L375
